propositions: Gate operations (transition closed, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no output to stdout/stderr between invocation start and final verdict, creating indistinguishability from hung processes to supervisor stall watchdogs with default 600s budgets.

Local compute phases (material assembly prologue ~27s, overlap corpus retrieval ~40s) and the LLM model call together routinely exceed common supervisor stall timeouts while silent, killing otherwise successful runs mid-close and leaving epic/story state corrupted.

No progress heartbeat, streaming output, or documented wall-clock duration bounds exist for gate operations, violating the contract that gates are the sanctioned path for autonomous agent close workflows.

ADR 0089 and test suite (test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism, test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout) establish that silence-tolerance is intentional design, so a fix must emit progress purely additively without introducing total-runtime caps or truncation.

A periodic liveness emitter (threading-based heartbeat to stderr, 30s interval) wrapping gate operations at executor/runner level can break the failure without violating ADR 0089's defer of stream-event idle watchdog.

Documentation must warn that gate operations routinely exceed 600s supervisor budgets while silent, and advise operators how to raise stall watchdog timeouts, since no upfront wall-clock benchmark is claimed or feasible.
